title: What if you kept digging straight down?

hooks.text: What if you dug straight down and never stopped?
The deepest hole on Earth is only as wide as a dinner plate.
Humans dug for nineteen years and barely scratched the Earth.
At 12 kilometers down, the rock stops acting like rock.
How deep can a human actually dig?
In 1970, scientists tried to dig to the center of the Earth.

hookVariants.visual: Close on the blocky hero mid-swing: the grass block under the pickaxe shatters and the camera tips down into the dark shaft.
Start INSIDE the shaft looking up at the hero's silhouette against the sky as blocks break toward the camera.
Wide top-down on the meadow: the hero is tiny, a square hole opens under the pickaxe, camera dives in.

beats.text: What if you dug straight down and never *stopped?*
beats.visual: Sunny voxel meadow. The hero swings a pickaxe; blocks under their feet crack and burst; on 'down' the camera tips over the edge and dives into the shaft.

beats.text: In 1970, Soviet scientists tried it for *real.*
beats.visual: Snowy tundra. A tall block-built drilling tower; two scientists in lab coats and hard hats; a pixel tag '1970' pops.

beats.text: Their hole was just 23 centimeters wide, about the size of a *dinner plate.*
beats.visual: Push in to the base of the tower: a narrow steel pipe goes into a small dark hole; a white dinner plate drops beside it, same width; tag '23 cm'.

beats.text: For nineteen years, the drill went down. One kilometer. *Five.* Ten.
beats.visual: Cutaway of the ground: grass, dirt, stone, deep stone. The drill bit spins downward past ore; a depth gauge counts 1, 5, 10 km as the camera follows.

beats.text: At 12,262 meters, it became the *deepest* hole humans have ever made.
beats.visual: The gauge slams to 12,262 m; the drill stops; a 'goal reached' toast slides in: DEEPEST HOLE.
Deep dark rock around the drill bit; the walls start to glow red; the picture gets hotter.

beats.text: The rock was 180 degrees Celsius, far hotter than anyone *expected.*
beats.visual: A pixel thermometer fills to the top; the number counts to 180 °C; magma veins light up in the walls.

beats.text: You see, at that heat, rock stops acting like rock. It starts to behave like *plastic.*
beats.visual: Close on the drill bit: the stone blocks around it soften, sag and wobble like jelly; tag 'LIKE PLASTIC'.

beats.text: The drill simply could not go any *deeper.*
beats.visual: The drill bit grinds, sparks, and stops; a red cross pops.

beats.text: So how far did they get? The center of the Earth is 6,371 kilometers *down.*
beats.visual: Pull way back: a cutaway voxel planet with crust, mantle and a glowing core; a line from the surface to the core counts 6,371 km.

beats.text: After nineteen years of digging, they made it *0.2 percent* of the way.
beats.visual: A tiny red notch on the planet's surface blinks: that is the hole. Big counter: 0.2 %. The hero from frame 0 stands on top, looks down, shrugs.
